entries.clue: Walking dead of medieval chronicles, named from the French for 'coming back'.
Flesh-eating demon of Arabic tales that prowls burial grounds by night.
Night of 31 October when the dead were said to walk abroad.
French for water, and the first word on countless fragrance labels.
Small glass tube holding a sample dose of something precious.
Volatile plant liquid carrying the smell, pressed from peel or distilled from petals.
Immortal part of a person, said to depart with the last breath.
White star-shaped flower picked before sunrise, when its smell is strongest.
Fibrous dried gourd used to buff away rough skin in the bath
Filmy white emanation of the darkened seance room, often exposed as cheesecloth.
Salon process of rods and waving lotion that leaves lasting curls
Treatment of soaking, filing and painting that smartens the hands
